points.heading: Deepen: two-word times
points.body:
Today we work only the **two-word** path. Piece one is **haber** conjugated (he, has, ha, habíamos…). Piece two is the **participle**, the already-done form in -ado or -ido. If you remember those two pieces, the rest is practice. English often uses «have sung» the same way Spanish uses **he cantado**—two words, helper plus done-form. Listen to the same participle **cantado** with different helpers: **he cantado** (done and still matters now); **había cantado** (done before another past); **habré cantado** (will be done by a future point); **habría cantado** (would already be done, like a guess). The participle stays; only the helper moves. Compare **Ayer comí** (one closed word) with **Ya he comido** (two words, result still alive)—same meal story, different path. Underline the participle every time so your eyes learn to spot the done-form quickly and surely.

Práctica: Ahora te toca a ti.

lesson.weekRecap: One word: canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría. Two words: helper haber + participle (he cantado). Learn to narrate WHEN an action happens: one-word forms and two-word forms, choosing with meaning.
